name: Color Me Beautiful
description: Heritage color-analysis beauty brand selling makeup and skincare organized by seasonal color palettes; its own affiliate program page states 25% commission on all affiliate sales and 'no limit to what you can earn.'

evidence.summary: Color Me Beautiful's own affiliate program page states: '25% commission on all affiliate sales (top of the industry), no limit to what you can earn', plus exclusive product sneak peeks and potential gifted PR/product that affiliates can request in the sign-up form. Joining is a 4-step interest-form process: join, get approved by the CMB or Flori Roberts team, start promoting with a unique URL and creative assets, earn on every qualified purchase. The 'no limit to what you can earn' statement on the program page itself makes the earnings cap verified uncapped.

The brand's own blog guide repeats the terms: '25% Commission on All Sales' and 'No Earnings Cap: There's no ceiling on your potential. The more you promote, the more you can earn.' It also states no huge following is needed, and gives the brand's credibility history: Color Me Beautiful has helped over 26 million women, popularized color analysis with its book of the same name plus six additional books, and sells through Seasonal Boutiques organized by palette.
No hard absolute creator count for Color Me Beautiful surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.niche_fit: Color-season makeup and skincare is built for try-on and palette-reveal UGC, and the program also covers sister brand Flori Roberts.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Own-site affiliate program with unique URLs, creative assets, sneak peeks and gifted-product requests inside the sign-up form; no hard creator count published.
reasons.compensation: 25% on all sales with 'no limit to what you can earn' stated on the program page itself - the strongest verified-uncapped rate in this round.
reasons.contact_access: Interest form on the brand's own program page; no public partnerships email was published on the pages fetched.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Applications open via the interest form with team review; the brand says no huge following is required.
reasons.credibility: Decades-old color-analysis authority claiming 26 million women helped and seven published books on color and makeup.

name: CLEARSTEM
description: Skincare brand targeting acne and aging at the same time with ingredient-transparent formulas; its Ambassador affiliate route runs on Impact, and the brand's own Terms of Service state there is no cap on the total commissions an Ambassador can earn from each order.

evidence.summary: CLEARSTEM's own Terms of Service (last update August 3, 2026), in the Ambassador obligations section, state: 'Ambassadors earn a commission on each order placed by consumers directed to CLEARSTEM Skincare Inc. by an Ambassador affiliate link...' and 'there is no cap on the total commissions an Ambassador can earn from each order attributed to their promotions.' The earnings-cap statement is therefore recorded as uncapped on the brand's own legal terms, quoted exactly; note the wording is framed per order attributed to the Ambassador's promotions.

AffiliateGraph's network-listing summary (updated Nov 9, 2026) lists CLEARSTEM on Impact as the direct network (Digidip and Skimlinks as sub-affiliates), with a listed commission range of 3%-25% and a stated base of 20% on online sales, while other directories list 10% (CompareEPC, LinkClicky). Because the published rates conflict across sources, commission_rate is recorded as null rather than settled.
No hard absolute creator count for CLEARSTEM surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.niche_fit: Acne-plus-aging positioning with ingredient transparency is proven skincare-UGC material with strong before/after potential.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A formal Ambassador structure in the brand's own terms plus a direct Impact network listing; no hard creator count published.
reasons.compensation: Earnings cap is verified uncapped in the brand's own Terms, but the percentage conflicts across network listings (3%-25% range, 20% base, 10% elsewhere), so the rate is honestly null.
reasons.contact_access: Ambassador page referenced in the brand's own Terms and application through Impact; no public partnerships email on the pages fetched.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Ambassador obligations are set by a Partnerships Manager per the Terms, so entry is managed rather than instant.
reasons.credibility: Established DTC skincare brand founded in 2017 by an acne specialist and a holistic nutritionist, per its Sovrn merchant profile.

name: Solid Actives
description: Premium solid-form skincare brand whose own Partner Program pays creators and skincare professionals 20% commission on the paid amount via a custom promo code, with audiences receiving 10% off.

evidence.summary: Solid Actives' own Partner Program page states partners earn '20% Commission Earned' with '10% Off for Your Audience', worked example included ($89 order - 10% code = $80.10 paid, 20% = $16.02 commission). It explicitly recruits 'Beauty & Wellness Creators' alongside aestheticians and editorial platforms, reviews applications personally within 3-5 business days, and activates a custom promo code on approval. The page publishes no earnings-cap statement, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown, never guessed.
The brand says it curates its partner network carefully, but publishes no absolute creator count, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.niche_fit: Premium solid-format actives are distinctive, demo-friendly skincare content for beauty and wellness creators.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Own-site partner program explicitly recruiting beauty and wellness creators with a worked commission example; no hard creator count published.
reasons.compensation: 20% on the post-discount paid amount is strong; no cap statement is published, so the cap is honestly unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Application on the brand's own partner page with personal review in 3-5 business days; no public email on the page fetched.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Curated approval against stated partnership standards (aesthetic alignment, accurate representation), so entry is selective.
reasons.credibility: Small premium brand with a detailed, transparent program page; limited third-party footprint.

name: BK Beauty
description: Creator-founded cosmetics brand (makeup brushes, tools and makeup) built by YouTube creator Lisa J; its affiliate program on ShareASale/Awin pays 15% commission on all sales with a +$100 average order value.

evidence.summary: BK Beauty's Awin merchant profile states: 'Our affiliate program offers 15% commission on all sales and our online store has a +$100 average order value', and describes BK Beauty as a direct-to-consumer cosmetics brand built and fueled by YouTube content creators and influencers. LinkClicky's directory independently lists the program on ShareASale at 15% per sale with a 30-day cookie. No earnings-cap statement was found on the pages fetched, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown, never guessed.

Digital Commerce 360 reported BK Beauty's affiliate program at 15% commission per product sold via a creator's link and that the program drove about 30% of the brand's sales, corroborating both the rate and the program's centrality. A separate founder interview states direct ShareASale sign-ups receive the full 15% while sub-affiliate networks take a cut.

A founder interview mentioned working with 'over 100 folks' in the program in 2022, but that figure is dated and not a current hard count, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than low.

reasons.niche_fit: Brushes and makeup from a creator-founded brand are native tutorial and review UGC material.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Affiliate-led brand from launch: program on ShareASale and Awin, reported at roughly 30% of brand sales, with product seeding described by the founder.
reasons.compensation: 15% on all sales against a +$100 average order value is solid per-sale economics; cap is honestly unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Joinable through the Awin merchant profile and ShareASale; no public partnerships email on the pages fetched.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open network application on two major networks.
reasons.credibility: Established DTC cosmetics brand with trade-press coverage of its affiliate-led growth.

name: L'Avyanna Beauty
description: Science-led skincare brand for melanin-rich skin with a free own-site affiliate program: 7.5% commission for Beauty Enthusiast affiliates and 15% for Influencer affiliates, plus a 5% audience discount code.

evidence.summary: L'Avyanna's own Affiliate Programme page states joining the affiliate program is free via the on-page form: affiliates share a unique link, give customers a 5% discount, and 'receive a commission ranging from 7.5% to 15% based on your engagement strength' - Category 1 Beauty Enthusiasts earn 7.5% and Category 2 Influencer Affiliates earn 15%, with dashboard access, marketing materials and, for influencers, priority support and collaboration opportunities. The page also lists info@lavyanna.com for its distributor route. Its 'unlimited opportunities' headline refers to the distributor packages, not an earnings-cap statement, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown, never guessed. The recorded rate is the 7.5% floor.
No hard absolute creator count for L'Avyanna surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.niche_fit: Science-led skincare formulated for melanin-rich skin is a clear, underserved UGC niche with strong routine content potential.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Own-site affiliate programme with two creator tiers, dashboard, personalized links and marketing materials; no hard creator count published.
reasons.compensation: 7.5% entry tier rising to 15% for influencer affiliates is modest; cap is honestly unknown - the page's 'unlimited' wording is about distributor opportunity, not earnings.
reasons.contact_access: Published brand email (info@lavyanna.com) plus the free on-page affiliate form.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free to join with a basic tier requiring only an active social account or blog.
reasons.credibility: Niche specialist brand with a detailed programme page; limited third-party footprint, and its paid distributor/stockist packages sit alongside the free affiliate route.

name: Rejuvaform

reasons.compensation: 15% monthly commission on all products plus free product and a 20% personal discount; cap is honestly unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Published email (hello@rejuvaform.com) plus the application form linked from the program page.

reasons.credibility: Made-in-Canada, vegan and cruelty-free positioning stated on the page; small brand with limited third-party footprint.

name: Care to Beauty
description: Beauty retailer selling skincare and cosmetics across international stores, running its own creators affiliate program: apply on-site, get manually reviewed within 48 business hours, and earn commission on every confirmed order through custom product and category links.

evidence.summary: Care to Beauty's own USA creators page describes its affiliate program: 'No paperwork, no minimum following, no exclusivity. Just apply, share, earn!' Applications are reviewed manually within 48 business hours; affiliates generate custom links for specific products, brands or categories, earn commission on every confirmed order, and cash out as in-store credit (no minimum) or bank transfer. Base rates are not published - the page says campaign boosts vary and 'You'll always see the active rate next to each link in your dashboard' - so commission_rate is recorded as null. The page publishes no earnings-cap statement, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown, never guessed. The program explicitly offers no gifted products or paid content, commission only.
No hard absolute creator count for Care to Beauty surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.niche_fit: A multi-brand beauty retailer lets creators monetize almost any skincare or makeup routine content through custom links.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Own creators program with custom link generation and a real-time earnings dashboard; explicitly commission-only with no gifting, and no hard creator count published.
reasons.compensation: Rates are only visible inside the dashboard and vary by campaign, so the rate is honestly null; cap unknown.
reasons.contact_access: On-site application form with manual review promised within 48 business hours; no public partnerships email on the page fetched.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application with no minimum following and no exclusivity.
reasons.credibility: Established international beauty retailer with stores in multiple countries and detailed published program terms.
